loci.rationale: The 'correct' action validates the email and logs a 'correction' event but performs no UPDATE of cases.email; the corrected address is never persisted to the case row.
offer() builds the recipient from c['email'], the stored case row field; since correction never writes that field, subsequent offers use the stale address.
get_case re-reads the case row from SQLite per request, so the offer path depends entirely on the persisted email column being updated.
Each request opens a fresh SQLite connection and commits on context exit; persistence across reopening depends on an UPDATE being issued inside this transaction.
Entrypoint: POST /case/<id>/correct dispatches to store.action with op='correct', scoping the request to the target case id.
Offer entrypoint: GET /case/<id>/offer calls store.offer(db,c) and serializes the result, so the recipient comes from the stored row.
action() resolves the case by id and requires owner authorization for non-staff ops, scoping the correction to the target case and leaving other cases untouched.
UI exposes the 'correct' form to the owner with an email field, confirming the rectification path is reachable.
